answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a bond that only unlocks after a long season of useful work, like tending a garden: fake accounts planted in bulk wither because each one must earn reputation slowly, while a cipher-signed work log proves the history belongs to one operator, and a shared atlas of verified attestations lets peers check that history before trusting a newcomer. Creating thousands of identities then costs real time and capital, not just a script.
